title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In this 1966 letter to Tate, Grothendieck has been conjecturing (2.4–2.6) that for an abelian scheme A/S, the de Rham cohomology H^1_DR(A/S) carries a canonical absolute stratification. This would come from a group scheme G(A) (essentially the universal vector extension, with H(B) = its Lie algebra) that is independent, up to unique isomorphism, of the infinitesimal lift B chosen over a thickening T. Section 2.7, on the previous page, refutes this in characteristic p. Fix a stratification on M = H^1_DR that is functorial in A and compatible with base change. Then Frobenius M^(p) → M would be horizontal. At a point s where A_s has Hasse invariant zero (F^2 = 0 on H^1_DR(A_s)), this property would propagate through the infinitesimal neighbourhoods of s. That is false for the modular family.

This page draws two consequences.

(1) The theory of the chapter (and of 2.2) can only survive if one works throughout with isocrystals (crystals up to isogeny, i.e. tensored with Q). Grothendieck adds that even his own notion of isocrystal, defined in 1.13 as a stratification on a formal lift over W, may be too restrictive. One may need characteristic-0 stratifications that do not extend over the whole formal scheme over W(k). He says a careful analysis of the 'key computation' of Washnitzer–Monsky should settle this. In modern terms: the right coefficient objects are not crystals on the full formal p-adic lift but stratified modules on smaller rigid-analytic domains (tubes, or overconvergent neighbourhoods), i.e. convergent or overconvergent isocrystals.

(2) Section 2.8 asks for which abelian schemes, in positive characteristic, the independence of G(B) from the lift B holds. The bracketed conjecture reads: for an abelian variety A over a field k of characteristic p > 0, independence holds for all Artinian rings with residue field k if and only if A is ordinary (maximal p-rank). He notes:
- k need not be perfect, since the question is geometric;
- so the p-divisible group (he corrected 'formel' to 'p-divisible') need not split as étale × infinitesimal.
If true, infinitesimal lifts of ordinary abelian varieties would be described explicitly by lifting a filtration (the Hodge filtration) of a Dieudonné-type module. This would avoid the 2.7 obstruction and fit with Serre(–Tate)'s canonical lifts and moduli of ordinary abelian varieties. The page ends by saying the analogous statement over an arbitrary base with all fibres ordinary is certainly false, even for elliptic schemes, for the same reasons. The next page develops this via the modular curve and purity.

Later revision. The whole conjectural paragraph is struck through diagonally in pencil. The margin reads 'faux, n'est jamais vrai en car p>0 !'. This is consistent with modern knowledge. In characteristic p the Gauss–Manin connection on H^1_DR of the universal elliptic curve has nonzero (nilpotent) p-curvature even on the ordinary locus (Katz, via Kodaira–Spencer). So it admits no compatible stratification. More generally, crystalline invariance of the universal extension holds only on divided-power thickenings, not on arbitrary Artinian thickenings. The correct statement, for all p-divisible groups and not only ordinary ones, is Grothendieck–Messing theory: deformations along nilpotent PD-thickenings correspond to lifts of the Hodge filtration in the Dieudonné crystal.
errors: The 2.8 conjecture is false as stated, as Grothendieck himself later noted in the margin. Independence of G(B) from the lift over arbitrary Artinian rings fails in char p even for ordinary A. Crystalline invariance requires divided-power thickenings, and in char p the Gauss–Manin connection on the ordinary locus has nonzero p-curvature, so no stratification exists.
Restricting to ordinary A is unnecessary for the 'filtration-lifting' description once one restricts to PD-thickenings: Grothendieck–Messing works for all p-divisible groups.
Minor: 'la notion de isocristal' should be 'd'isocristal'; 'Notes qu'il' presumably 'Notons qu'il'.

ideas.what: Passing from crystals to isocrystals to repair the failure of canonical stratifications on H^1_DR in char p
ideas.modern_name: F-isocrystals / crystalline cohomology tensored with Q
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968); ICM 1970 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux'

ideas.what: Suspicion that isocrystals defined as stratifications on the full formal lift over W are too restrictive; one should allow char-0 stratifications not extending over the whole formal scheme, to be clarified by analysing Washnitzer–Monsky
ideas.modern_name: Convergent and overconvergent isocrystals; rigid cohomology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ogus (convergent isocrystals, 1984); Berthelot (rigid cohomology, overconvergent isocrystals, 1980s); building on Monsky–Washnitzer and Dwork
ideas.where_published: unsure; possibly only in this letter to Tate

ideas.what: Conjecture: independence of the universal-extension group G(B) from the infinitesimal lift holds over Artinian rings iff A is ordinary; then lifts are described by lifting a filtration of a Dieudonné module
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Messing deformation theory (correct over PD-thickenings, for all p-divisible groups); Serre–Tate theory for ordinary abelian varieties

ideas.what: Remark that over imperfect k the p-divisible group of an ordinary A need not split as étale × infinitesimal, yet the question is geometric
ideas.modern_name: Non-split connected–étale sequence over imperfect fields

ideas.what: Failure over a general base with all fibres ordinary, even for elliptic schemes
ideas.modern_name: Nonvanishing p-curvature of Gauss–Manin on the ordinary locus / failure of canonical stratification

missed.claim: Already in 1966 Grothendieck suspected that the right isocrystals are char-0 stratifications that need not extend over the whole formal scheme over W. He pointed to the Washnitzer–Monsky computation as the key to deciding this, i.e. an anticipation of convergent/overconvergent isocrystals and rigid cohomology roughly 15 years early.
missed.quote: il faudra peut-être prendre des stratifications en caractéristique nulle qui ne se prolongeraient pas nécessairement sur le schéma formel sur W = vecteurs de Witt tout entier. C'est une analyse soigneuse du calcul-clef de Washnitzer-Monsky qui devrait permettre de tirer cette question au clair.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The history of rigid cohomology usually credits Berthelot, Ogus and Monsky–Washnitzer/Dwork. An explicit early Grothendieck pointer to overconvergence via Monsky–Washnitzer is a historically relevant precursor, though not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The isocrystal remark is a genuine early anticipation of convergent/overconvergent isocrystals tied explicitly to Monsky–Washnitzer, but it is only a hint, not a construction. The rest is a struck-out conjecture, self-corrected as false, whose correct form (Grothendieck–Messing) is well known and credited to Grothendieck.
